content.title: About
content.content: Taquito are small crunchy rolls made from a corn or wheat tortilla, filled with tender chicken fillet, spices and sometimes vegetables. The product is popular in Mexican cuisine as a quick snack or appetizer.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Taquito are often served with salsa, guacamole or sour cream.
Traditionally the rolls are made from corn tortillas, but some regions use a wheat base.
The chicken filling is usually marinated in chili, paprika and lime spices.
In the United States Taquito are frequently sold frozen, ready for microwave or oven heating.
The name “taquito” comes from the Spanish word meaning “little taco”.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken meat is a good source of high‑quality protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other snacks, chicken Taquito contain less saturated fat, especially when prepared without excess oil.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken provides vitamin B6 and niacin, which support metabolism and the nervous system.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: The product supplies iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood formation and bones.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: Chicken meat is considered easy to digest, making Taquito a suitable snack for children and older adults.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to poultry, experiencing skin reactions or breathing difficulties.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Ready‑made Taquito often contain added salt and sauces, increasing sodium levels.

items.title: Trans fats in coating
items.content: Industrial breadings may contain trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Risk of food poisoning
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking of chicken can lead to bacterial growth such as salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Taquito can be heated in the oven, microwave or skillet until golden and crisp. Serve with salsa, guacamole, sour cream or fresh lime. They are convenient to eat by hand as a snack or added to a salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen Taquito in the freezer at –18 °C. After thawing, cook immediately. Cooked rolls can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days.
